questions.subtopic: Heart failure and poor weight gain
questions.stemEn: A 5-month-old infant has heart failure and is receiving furosemide and lisinopril. His weight is low. What is the best option to improve weight gain?
questions.explanationAr: المصدر يوضح أن الطفل المصاب بـheart failure قد تكون احتياجاته الحرارية مرتفعة ويتعب أثناء الرضاعة، وإذا تعذر الوصول إلى caloric target بالفم فقد يحتاج nasogastric feeding. لذلك اختار المصدر NGT feeding.
questions.reasoningEn: The source states that children with heart failure may have increased caloric needs and limited oral intake, and that nasogastric or gastrostomy feeds may be required to achieve adequate intake.
questions.incorrectOptionsAr: MCT oil قد يزيد كثافة السعرات لكنه لا يحل مشكلة عدم القدرة على الوصول للهدف الحراري إذا كان oral intake غير كافٍ. Introducing solids ليس الحل الرئيسي في هذا العمر والحالة. TPN أكثر تدخلاً ولا يختاره المصدر عندما يمكن استخدام enteral feeding.
questions.clinicalPearl: In infants with heart failure who cannot meet caloric targets orally, enteral tube feeding may be required.
managementSteps: Use enteral tube feeding when oral intake cannot meet needs

tts.text: A five-month-old infant has heart failure and is receiving furosemide and lisinopril. His weight is low. What is the best option to improve weight gain? A. Add MCT oil. B. Introduce solid feeding. C. Start nasogastric tube feeding. D. Start total parenteral nutrition.

questions.stemEn: An infant has just been diagnosed with intestinal lymphangiectasia. Which dietary advice is most appropriate?

options.text: Diet mainly consisting of protein and MCT oil

questions.explanationAr: المصدر يذكر أن mainstay of dietary therapy في primary intestinal lymphangiectasia هو low-fat, high-protein diet مع medium-chain triglycerides (MCT)، لذلك الخيار A هو المقصود.
questions.reasoningEn: The source describes a low-fat, high-protein, high-MCT diet as the mainstay of dietary therapy for primary intestinal lymphangiectasia.
questions.incorrectOptionsAr: إضافة carbohydrates وحدها لا تعالج فقد البروتين واللمف ولا تمثل الحمية الأساسية المذكورة في المصدر.
questions.clinicalPearl: Primary intestinal lymphangiectasia: low-fat, high-protein diet with MCT.

tts.text: An infant has just been diagnosed with intestinal lymphangiectasia. Which dietary advice is most appropriate? A. A diet mainly consisting of protein and MCT oil. B. Add carbohydrates to the diet.

questions.stemEn: A child adopted from Africa presents with headache, visual problems, and a white eye lesion described as Bitot's spots. Which vitamin deficiency is most likely?
questions.explanationAr: Bitot's spots من علامات xerophthalmia المرتبطة بـVitamin A deficiency، والمصدر يختار Retinol (Vitamin A).
questions.reasoningEn: The source identifies Bitot's spots as part of xerophthalmia due to vitamin A deficiency.
questions.clinicalPearl: Bitot's spots are a classic clue to vitamin A deficiency.

tts.text: A child adopted from Africa presents with headache, visual problems, and a white eye lesion described as Bitot's spots. Which vitamin deficiency is most likely? A. Retinol, Vitamin A.

questions.stemEn: A mother of a 2-year-old girl asks how you will assess her nutritional status. Which measure is most appropriate?
questions.explanationAr: المصدر يختار weight-for-height ويشرح أنه مؤشر يفيد في تقييم wasting، كما يذكر أن weight-for-height يُستخدم سريريًا خصوصًا في الأطفال الأصغر سنًا، بينما BMI يصبح المعيار المعتاد بعد عمر سنتين.
questions.reasoningEn: The source key is weight-for-height and its explanation discusses weight-for-height as an anthropometric indicator of wasting and nutritional status.
questions.incorrectOptionsAr: Weight alone لا يفرق بين wasting وstunting. Skinfold measurements أقل دقة وتكرارية بحسب شرح المصدر. Calorie calculation لا يحل محل القياسات الأنثروبومترية.
questions.clinicalPearl: Interpret anthropometry in the context of age; the source tests weight-for-height here.

tts.text: A mother of a two-year-old girl asks how you will assess her nutritional status. Which measure is most appropriate? A. Weight measurement only. B. Weight for height. C. Skinfold thickness. D. Calorie calculation.

questions.stemEn: A 5-month-old infant with failure to thrive did not improve with high-calorie formula during outpatient follow-up. Weight remains below the 3rd percentile, and basic laboratory tests and review of systems are unremarkable. What will you do next?
questions.explanationAr: المصدر يختار admission بعد فشل outpatient nutritional intervention، ويذكر أن عدم الاستجابة بعد فترة من المتابعة قد يستدعي hospitalization لمراقبة التغذية، إعادة التقييم، وربما بدء nasogastric feeds ودراسة تفاعل الطفل مع مقدم الرعاية.
questions.reasoningEn: The source states that hospitalization may be considered when a child fails outpatient management, for observed feeding, further evaluation, and possible nasogastric feeding.
questions.incorrectOptionsAr: Referral وحده قد لا يحقق observed feeding وإعادة التقييم التي يستهدفها السؤال بعد فشل التدخل الخارجي. المصدر يختار admission في هذا السيناريو.
questions.clinicalPearl: Failure of structured outpatient nutritional management may justify admission for observed feeding and re-evaluation.
managementSteps: Admit for observed feeding and reassessment when outpatient intervention has failed
Consider further diagnostic evaluation and enteral support as needed

questions.stemEn: Which of the following is a major criterion to diagnose anorexia nervosa?

options.text: Use of medication to lose weight

questions.explanationAr: المصدر يختار intense fear of gaining weight كعلامة أساسية في anorexia nervosa. Amenorrhea قد تظهر سريريًا لكنها ليست الخيار الذي اختبره المصدر كمعيار رئيسي هنا.
questions.reasoningEn: The source key is intense fear of gaining weight and links the question to anorexia nervosa diagnostic features.
questions.incorrectOptionsAr: Medication use قد يحدث في بعض الأنماط لكنه ليس المعيار الرئيسي المقصود في السؤال. Amenorrhea قد تكون من المضاعفات/السمات لكنها ليست الإجابة المختبرة هنا.
questions.clinicalPearl: Intense fear of weight gain is a core anorexia nervosa feature in the source question.

tts.text: Which of the following is a major criterion to diagnose anorexia nervosa? A. Intense fear of gaining weight. B. Use of medication to lose weight. C. Amenorrhea.

questions.stemEn: A young female presents with an eating disorder. Which of the following will support a diagnosis of anorexia nervosa?

options.text: She drinks a large amount of water

questions.explanationAr: المصدر يختار laxative abuse، لكنه لا يقدم شرحًا تفصيليًا لهذا السؤال ويكتفي بالإحالة للسؤال السابق. لذلك نحفظ مفتاح الـrecall كما هو ولا نرفعه إلى verified answer بدون مراجعة مستقلة.
questions.reasoningEn: The compilation keys laxative abuse but provides no specific explanation beyond referring to the preceding anorexia question.
questions.incorrectOptionsAr: المصدر لا يقدم تفصيلًا كافيًا لمقارنة الخيارات في هذا السؤال، لذلك لا نضيف تعليلًا غير موجود في المادة الأصلية.
questions.clinicalPearl: Recalled key preserved; independent review is required because the source explanation is insufficient.

questions.stemEn: A 13-year-old girl has poor oral intake, very low BMI, and sees herself as obese. She is admitted to the hospital. Which finding would you expect?
questions.explanationAr: المصدر يذكر أن moderate to severe anorexia nervosa قد تسبب gastroparesis أو delayed gastric emptying مع early satiety وbloating. لذلك اختار C. كما ينبه أن metabolic alkalosis ترتبط أكثر بوجود vomiting أو بعض سلوكيات purging.
questions.reasoningEn: The source explanation states that moderate to severe anorexia nervosa consistently causes gastroparesis/delayed gastric emptying.
questions.incorrectOptionsAr: المصدر يذكر أن metabolic alkalosis قد تُرى عند severe vomiting أو purging، لكنها ليست finding المفترض من السيناريو وحده. Hypernatremia وSVT ليست الإجابة التي يدعمها شرح المصدر.
questions.clinicalPearl: Food restriction and significant weight loss can be associated with delayed gastric emptying.

tts.text: A thirteen-year-old girl has poor oral intake, very low BMI, and sees herself as obese. She is admitted to the hospital. Which finding would you expect? A. Hypernatremia. B. Metabolic alkalosis. C. Delayed gastric emptying. D. Supraventricular tachycardia.

questions.stemEn: Which of the following is a recommended intervention in the treatment of anorexia nervosa?
questions.explanationAr: المصدر يذكر أن family-based treatment مثل Maudsley approach هو العلاج الذي لديه evidence-based effectiveness في الأطفال والمراهقين، ولذلك يختار Family therapy.
questions.reasoningEn: The source states that family-based treatment, exemplified by the Maudsley approach, has evidence-based effectiveness in children and adolescents with anorexia nervosa.
questions.incorrectOptionsAr: المصدر يذكر أن interpersonal وpsychoanalytic approaches أقل فعالية، وأن group therapy قد يوفر دعمًا لكنه يحتاج skilled clinician ولا يمثل الإجابة الأفضل هنا.
questions.clinicalPearl: Family-based treatment is emphasized by the source for adolescents with anorexia nervosa.
managementSteps: Use family-based treatment as part of multidisciplinary care

questions.stemEn: A 14-year-old girl presents with fatigue and low weight. Her heart rate is 40 beats per minute, blood pressure is 80/50 mmHg, and laboratory tests show hypokalemia and hypomagnesemia. What will you do next?

options.text: IV hydration then discharge with follow-up after 48 hours

questions.explanationAr: المصدر يختار hospital admission في وجود marked bradycardia، hypotension، وelectrolyte abnormalities. هذه الصورة في السؤال تمثل medical instability وليست حالة مناسبة للمتابعة الخارجية فقط.
questions.reasoningEn: The source key is hospital admission for the medically unstable adolescent described by severe bradycardia, hypotension, and electrolyte abnormalities.
questions.incorrectOptionsAr: Dietitian أو psychiatry referral قد يكونان جزءًا من الخطة لاحقًا، لكن المصدر يختبر الأولوية الطبية الفورية. IV hydration ثم discharge لا يتوافق مع شدة instability الموجودة في stem.
questions.clinicalPearl: Medical instability in an eating disorder requires inpatient medical management in the source question.

tts.text: A fourteen-year-old girl presents with fatigue and low weight. Her heart rate is forty beats per minute, blood pressure is eighty over fifty millimeters of mercury, and laboratory tests show hypokalemia and hypomagnesemia. What will you do next? A. Hospital admission. B. Dietitian referral. C. Urgent psychiatry referral. D. Intravenous hydration then discharge with follow-up after forty-eight hours.
